I believe "Black Eye" refers to either an existing DARPA program called RADICS or "Black Eye" is the name of the now operational RADICS development program.

DARPA (Defense Advanced Research Programs Agency) is a DoD technology development agency that attempts to look out 10-20 years at what technologies the military might need. A large part of DARPA is just pure preliminary research where developers (i.e, universities and companies bid on DARPA proposed contracts and the winning teams compete to develop the viable technology) produce proof of concept technologies that may or may not be further developed and transitioned to one or more of the services.

For example, the stealth technology for the F-117 stealth fighter was developed jointly by DARPA and the Air Force using universities and private companies. That happened to be a top secret program. Most DARPA contracts are unclassified because universities have so many foreign students that they would have trouble fielding an all US development team. I was a consultant to a number of DARPA programs for 15 years. About half of every development team working on unclassified technologies are foreign students attending US universities.

Anyway, RADICS stands for Rapid Attack Detection, Isolation and Characterization System which was to develop automated systems to deal with a loss of power on our electric grid, such as a massive cyber attack or an EMP attack. It was originally designed to help utilities engineers to restore power within seven days of an attack.

RADICS called for the design of a secure emergency network that could connect power suppliers in the moments after an attack.

I could go on, but you get the idea. RADICS tries to forecast an attack by monitoring the grid dynamic, limit the loss of power during an attack, and restoring power as soon as possible after an attack.

This was all going on a few years ago, so Black Eye, in my opinion, is most likely the military adaptation of DARPA RADICS. It seems to fit Q's context.
